caption: R5 000 of my salary goes to a mistake I made in one bad week online. How long did it take you to admit you'd been scammed?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R23 500
p/m salary
Living in Vryheid
slides.body:
Female, 26
Single, no kids
Job: Office administrator
Net salary: R23 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: Small town rent. It still eats a third of what I actually get to keep after debt.

slides.title: Credit card
slides.body: Started as one online order. It didn't stay that way.

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: R32 000 balance, 25% interest, 18 months left, taken out after I paid a 'supplier' that turned out to be a scam
slides.body: I still feel stupid saying it out loud. The loan doesn't care how it happened.

slides.title: Store account
slides.body: Felt like nothing at R299 a month. It's R900 once you add the second item.

slides.title: Takeaways & coffee
slides.includes: Office coffee runs, Friday lunch with the team
slides.body: I guessed R400. It was R750. Bad months make you buy more coffee.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Groceries, petrol & insurance, medical aid, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, savings
slides.body: R12 150 that isn't debt and isn't rent. It's the only part of this I can actually move.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R23 500. R5 000 of that goes to the card, the loan and the store account. At this pace the store account clears in 7 months, the card in 12, the loan in 18.

slides.title: I stopped avoiding what I owe
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

Seeing the three repayments added up on one screen was worse, and more useful, than any of them alone.

No bank login needed.
